Privileged or root pod created by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount AIInstallation High
Detects the Kubernetes-API-server-side effect of CVE-2026-44182: a Pod created by the enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount whose spec contains `privileged: true`, `runAsUser: 0`, `runAsGroup: 0`, a `hostPath` mount, or `hostNetwork: true`. EG should only ever spawn unprivileged kernel pods running as uid 1000 (jovyan); any privileged spec from this SA is the post-injection footprint. Rationale: Anchors on the EG-default identity (the `enterprise-gateway` ServiceAccount, see Helm chart) and the article-stated effects: the PoC explicitly produces pods with `privileged:true, runAsUser:0, runAsGroup:0` and notes the impact extends to arbitrary `hostPath` mounts. Normal EG kernel pods run as `uid=1000(jovyan)` per the rendered template — any privileged/root spec from this SA is the injection footprint, not noise. Only the original GHSA cross-checked. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfw7-6c5v-2wjq • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/kernel-pod.yaml.j2#L77 • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/launch_kubernetes.py#L130-L137
ATT&CKT1611 T1068 T1190
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator-driven EG redeploy that legitimately needs `hostPath` for a custom kernel image (should appear in change tickets)
  • Cluster admins testing EG with a non-default kernel launcher that sets `runAsUser: 0` intentionally for a GPU-pinned kernel
  • Kustomize/Helm upgrade where EG SA temporarily reapplies a kernel-pod template that includes a deprecated `securityContext` block
  • Pod Security Admission webhook re-emits the requestObject during validation, double-logging the same create
  • Internal scanner (kube-bench, Falco rule replay) replaying a known privileged-pod manifest against EG SA in a test namespace
Suppression filter
| where Caller !has "system:serviceaccount:kube-system" | where not(RequestObject has "gpu" and RequestObject has "nvidia.com/gpu") | where Namespace !in ("eg-staging", "eg-test", "sandbox-notebooks")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the matched AKSAudit/CloudTrail record, extract `objectRef.name` and `objectRef.namespace`, and confirm the requestObject contains a privileged field that was not in any pinned EG template (compare against the Helm-rendered baseline). Capture the source IP from `sourceIPs[]`. 2) Contain: delete the offending pod (`kubectl delete pod -n <ns> <name>`), cordon the node it landed on, scale `enterprise-gateway` to 0, and rotate the EG ServiceAccount token + kernel-namespace ServiceAccount tokens. If `hostPath` was mounted, treat the node as compromised and reimage. 3) Hunt: enumerate every pod the EG SA has created in the last 30 days where `runAsUser==0` or `privileged==true` or any `hostPath`; pull egress flow logs from those pod IPs for C2 indicators; check the EG ingress access logs for `/api/kernels` POSTs with `KERNEL_*` injection markers and pivot back to UC1.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb == "create"
| where tostring(ObjectRef) has "\"resource\":\"pods\""
| where Stage == "ResponseComplete"
| where tostring(User) has_any ("enterprise-gateway", "enterprise_gateway")
| where tostring(RequestObject) has_any ("\"privileged\":true", "\"runAsUser\":0", "\"runAsGroup\":0", "\"hostNetwork\":true", "\"hostPID\":true", "hostPath")
| extend PodName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).name)
| extend Namespace = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).namespace)
| extend Caller = tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Caller, Namespace, PodName, Verb, RequestUri, RequestObject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Privileged Pod Created by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount (CVE-2026-44182)
id: 7e2a9c4b-1d8f-4a3e-9b6c-5f0a8d2e1c7f
description: Detects pod creation by the enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount whose spec contains privileged true, runAsUser 0, hostNetwork true, hostPID true, or a hostPath volume — the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-44182 Jinja2 YAML injection.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfw7-6c5v-2wjq
  - https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/kernel-pod.yaml.j2#L77
author: ucs-pipeline
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  product: kubernetes
  service: audit
detection:
  selection:
    verb: create
    objectRef.resource: pods
    stage: ResponseComplete
    user.username|contains: 'enterprise-gateway'
    requestObject|contains:
      - '"privileged":true'
      - '"runAsUser":0'
      - '"runAsGroup":0'
      - '"hostNetwork":true'
      - '"hostPID":true'
      - 'hostPath'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Intentional administrator override re-deployment of EG with privileged kernel launchers (rare and should already be on a change record)
level: high
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:create @objectRef.resource:pods @stage:ResponseComplete @user.username:*enterprise-gateway* (@requestObject.spec.securityContext.runAsUser:0 OR @requestObject.spec.securityContext.runAsGroup:0 OR @requestObject.spec.containers.securityContext.privileged:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostNetwork:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostPID:true OR @requestObject.spec.volumes.hostPath.path:*)
# log group: /aws/eks/<cluster-name>/cluster
fields @timestamp, verb, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, user.username, sourceIPs.0, requestObject.spec.hostNetwork, requestObject.spec.hostPID
| filter verb = "create"
      and objectRef.resource = "pods"
      and stage = "ResponseComplete"
      and user.username like /enterprise-gateway/
      and (@message like /"privileged":true/
           or @message like /"runAsUser":0/
           or @message like /"runAsGroup":0/
           or @message like /"hostNetwork":true/
           or @message like /"hostPID":true/
           or @message like /hostPath/)
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
CLOUD
search (sourcetype=kube:apiserver:audit OR sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs:eks" OR sourcetype="aks:audit" OR sourcetype="gcp:gke:audit")
  verb=create "objectRef.resource"=pods stage=ResponseComplete
  ("user.username"=*enterprise-gateway* OR "user.username"="system:serviceaccount:enterprise-gateway:enterprise-gateway*" OR "impersonatedUser.username"=*enterprise-gateway*)
  ("\"privileged\":true" OR "\"runAsUser\":0" OR "\"runAsGroup\":0" OR "\"hostNetwork\":true" OR "\"hostPID\":true" OR "hostPath")

Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels (CVE-2026-44181) AIExploitation High
Hunts for HTTP POST requests targeting Jupyter Enterprise Gateway's /api/kernels endpoint carrying a Jinja2 server-side template injection payload in KERNEL_POD_NAME / KERNEL_WORKING_DIR / KERNEL_NAMESPACE fields. Specifically pivots on the Python sandbox-escape gadgets (cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen, __subclasses__, __builtins__) that the PoC and any real-world weaponization must include to reach OS-command execution. Rationale: All keywords (`/api/kernels`, `KERNEL_POD_NAME`, `KERNEL_WORKING_DIR`, `KERNEL_NAMESPACE`, `{{`, `cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen`, `__subclasses__`) are taken verbatim from the GHSA PoC. The combination of an EG endpoint URL plus Jinja2 mustache markers plus Python globals-walk gadgets has essentially zero benign explanation. Defender XDR cannot inspect inbound HTTP bodies, so defender_kql is empty by design; Falcon FDR likewise does not ship raw HTTP body content. CloudWatch is non-applicable (not AWS-specific telemetry). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w • https://github.com/swisskyrepo/PayloadsAllTheThings/blob/master/Server%20Side%20Template%20Injection/Python.md
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red-team / pentest exercise sending {{7*7}} or similar probes against EG
  • Authorised Nuclei / Burp / sqlmap scans hitting /api/kernels
  • Security researcher manually testing the CVE post-patch
  • WAF rule-tuning replay traffic from a SIEM appliance
  • Developer sending a literal `{{` character in a kernel display name (rare; no SSTI gadgets present)
Suppression filter
and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nuclei", "sqlmap", "Burp", "ZAP", "Acunetix") and SourceIP in ("<known-scanner-cidrs>"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full request body and confirm it contains a Jinja2 expression chained to `__globals__`, `os.popen`, `os.system`, or `cycler.__init__`. Resolve the source IP — internal scanner vs external attacker vs known partner. Check the EG version banner against the fixed release in GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w. 2. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter WAF; delete the Enterprise Gateway pod to force re-roll of its service-account token; revoke the SA's pod/secret/rolebinding RBAC verbs until patched; apply NetworkPolicy denying ingress to EG from outside the notebooks namespace. 3. Hunt: pivot to the K8s audit and EG-pod process telemetry (see sister UCs) — search for any pod creations by the EG SA bearing privileged/hostPath/hostNetwork over the last 90 days, and for python-spawned shells or SA-token reads on the EG node.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/api/kernels"
| where Message has_any ("KERNEL_POD_NAME", "KERNEL_WORKING_DIR", "KERNEL_NAMESPACE")
| where Message has "{{"
| where Message has_any ("__globals__", "__class__", "__mro__", "__subclasses__", "__builtins__", "cycler.__init__", "os.popen", "os.system", "subprocess", "__import__", "popen")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Enterprise Gateway service account creates privileged / hostPath / RBAC-escalating pod (CVE-2026-44181 post-exploit) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for Kubernetes API actions by the Jupyter Enterprise Gateway service account that fall outside its legitimate role of launching kernel pods: creating a pod with privileged securityContext, hostPath / hostNetwork / hostPID, or creating/updating rolebindings, clusterrolebindings, or reading cluster secrets. These are the textbook pivots after stealing the EG SA token via SSTI RCE, as the GHSA explicitly notes. Rationale: The GHSA explicitly enumerates the Enterprise Gateway SA's RBAC — including `pods [create]`, `secrets [get watch list]`, `rolebindings [create]` — and explicitly names the attacker's next step (schedule a privileged pod or hostPath-volume pod for cluster takeover). The detection ties three article-specific anchors together: actor identity (`enterprise-gateway` in the SA username), action verb (create/update on pods/rolebindings/secrets), and payload shape (`privileged:true`, `hostPath`, `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`) — the legitimate kernel-launcher YAML never includes any of those. Falcon LogScale is left empty because FDR does not ship K8s audit; Defender Advanced Hunting likewise has no K8s-audit table. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/kernel-pod.yaml.j2
ATT&CKT1611 T1078.004 T1552.005
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cluster admin impersonating the EG SA during troubleshooting (`kubectl --as=...`)
  • GitOps tooling (Argo, Flux) using a similarly-named SA to apply privileged DaemonSet specs
  • Helm upgrade of the EG chart itself rewriting its own RoleBinding
  • Operator-deployed init container that legitimately needs hostPath (e.g. log shipper) being launched under the EG SA
  • Backup jobs (Velero) impersonating SA to snapshot secrets
Suppression filter
| where not (UserAgent has_any ("argocd","helm","flux","velero") or RequestUri has "impersonate")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full RequestObject and confirm the offending field (privileged, hostPath path, hostNetwork, hostPID, or the RoleBinding subject). A legitimate Jupyter kernel pod has none of these — any hit is high-fidelity. Confirm sourceIPs is the EG pod IP (not an admin workstation), which indicates a stolen token rather than a misused impersonation. 2. Contain: delete the offending pod (`kubectl delete pod -n <ns> <name>`); rotate the EG service-account token (`kubectl delete secret <eg-sa-token> -n <ns>` plus pod re-roll); strip create verbs on rolebindings/clusterrolebindings from the EG ClusterRole pending patch; cordon the node hosting any pod that successfully mounted hostPath. 3. Hunt: query the last 90 days of K8s audit for any `get`/`list` on secrets by the EG SA (token-stealing reconnaissance); search for kubectl exec into pods sharing the same node; pivot to UC #3 to confirm SSTI execution on the EG pod itself.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend Username = coalesce(tostring(User.username), tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username))
| where Username has "enterprise-gateway"
| where Verb in~ ("create","update","patch")
| extend Resource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), Namespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace), TargetName = tostring(ObjectRef.name)
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where Resource in~ ("pods","rolebindings","clusterrolebindings","secrets")
| where (Resource == "pods" and (ReqStr has "hostPath" or ReqStr contains "\"privileged\":true" or ReqStr contains "\"hostNetwork\":true" or ReqStr contains "\"hostPID\":true"))
    or Resource in~ ("rolebindings","clusterrolebindings","secrets")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Username, Verb, Resource, Namespace, TargetName, RequestUri, ReqStr, ResponseStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Enterprise Gateway python container spawns shell or reads K8s service-account token (CVE-2026-44181 RCE) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the on-host signal of the SSTI RCE landing inside the Jupyter Enterprise Gateway pod: a python interpreter spawning a shell, recon binary, or curl/wget, or any process reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. The article's PoC uses `cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen('hostname')` — `os.popen` results in a python→sh→hostname process tree that is otherwise unheard-of for the EG service. Rationale: The PoC payload `cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen("hostname").read()` proves the exact process-tree shape the detection targets: python (the Enterprise Gateway service) → sh -c → hostname. The article also explicitly names theft of the Kubernetes service-account token (`/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`) as the attacker objective, so we additionally pivot on any python-parented process referencing that path. Host-scope filters (`enterprise-gateway` in hostname / pod name / container image) keep the signal tight to the vulnerable workload rather than every python process in the fleet. CloudWatch is empty (not CloudTrail/VPC-flow telemetry). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/enterprise_gateway/services/processproxies/k8s.py#L219-L247
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.004 T1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Jupyter kernel-launcher legitimately invoking subprocess to start a Python kernel (child is python, not sh — already excluded)
  • Container init script (e.g. tini → python entrypoint shell) running once at pod startup
  • Liveness probe shelling out via python wrapper to call /bin/true
  • Operator-injected debug sidecar (kubectl debug) under a python parent
  • Admin running `kubectl exec -ti <eg-pod> -- /bin/sh` for troubleshooting (interactive; suppress on TTY presence)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "jupyter-kernel" and FileName in~ ("python","python3") and ProcessCommandLine has "ipykernel_launcher")
| where not (FileName == "hostname" and ProcessCommandLine == "hostname" and ParentProcessName has "tini")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full process tree on the alerting node, confirm the EG pod's container image hash matches the vulnerable Enterprise Gateway version (pre-fix). Decode the child cmdline — `os.popen('hostname')` is the article's exact PoC; any string referencing `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` is unambiguous credential theft. 2. Contain: `kubectl delete pod <eg-pod>` to terminate the compromised process; rotate the EG service-account token at the API server; apply a NetworkPolicy denying egress from the EG namespace to anywhere except the K8s API server; block egress at the cluster gateway to non-corporate destinations. 3. Hunt: search the cluster's K8s audit (UC #2) for any pod creates / secret reads / rolebinding writes by the EG SA in the trailing 90 days; sweep all nodes for hostPath-mounted pods originating from EG; look for outbound DNS from the EG pod's IP to recently-registered or low-reputation domains; check for `/tmp/` or `/dev/shm/` writes by python o
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| where (FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","hostname","id","whoami","uname","curl","wget","nc","ncat","kubectl"))
    or ProcessCommandLine has "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("os.popen","os.system","subprocess.Popen")
| where DeviceName has_any ("enterprise-gateway","jupyter","jeg")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("tini","containerd-shim","runc","docker-init")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("enterprise_gateway","jupyter_enterprise_gateway")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
    or ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","ash","hostname","id","whoami","uname","curl","wget","nc","ncat","kubectl"))

    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("enterprise_gateway","jupyter_enterprise_gateway")

| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway Python Spawns Shell or Reads K8s SA Token (CVE-2026-44181)
id: 71a3b8f2-7d18-4a8b-a6c3-3b1f9b4b2a5c
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious child processes (shells, recon binaries) or Kubernetes service-account token reads from the python process running Jupyter Enterprise Gateway, indicative of SSTI RCE post-exploitation (CVE-2026-44181, GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f49j-v924-fx9w
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1552.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent_python:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/python3.10'
      - '/python3.11'
      - '/python3.12'
  suspicious_child_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/ash'
      - '/hostname'
      - '/id'
      - '/whoami'
      - '/uname'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/kubectl'
  token_read:
    CommandLine|contains: '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount'
  condition: parent_python and (suspicious_child_shell or token_read)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Jupyter kernel-launcher subprocess.Popen invocations to start a Python kernel (those launch python child, not sh/bash/curl)
  - Container init/healthcheck reading hostname (uncommon with python parent)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:(python OR python3) OR @process.parent.executable.path:*python*) (@process.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR ash OR hostname OR id OR whoami OR uname OR curl OR wget OR nc OR ncat OR kubectl) OR @process.command_line:*\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes.io\/serviceaccount* OR @process.command_line:(*os.popen* OR *os.system*)) (@host.name:*enterprise-gateway* OR @kube_pod_name:*enterprise-gateway* OR @kube_container_name:*enterprise-gateway*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^python3?(\.[0-9]+)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|ash|hostname|id|whoami|uname|curl|wget|nc|ncat|kubectl)$/i OR CommandLine=/\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount/i OR CommandLine=/os\.(popen|system)|subprocess\.Popen/i
| regex("enterprise[-_]?gateway|jupyter|jeg", field=ComputerName) OR regex("enterprise_gateway|jupyter_enterprise_gateway", field=ParentImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| count > 0

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44181")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44181")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
